document.title: Gandhi Letter to Reagan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Gandhi congratulates Reagan on the INF treaty and informs him of his meeting with Najibullah and Indian outreach to Zahir Shah and other groups inside and outside Afghanistan to facilitate a stable, representative political order.

persons.name: Rajiv Gandhi
persons.role: Prime Minister of India; author of the letter

mentions.quote: I had a meeting in Delhi today with Mr. Najibullah, who made a transit halt on his way to Vietnam.

persons.name: Ronald Reagan
persons.role: President of the United States; addressee

mentions.quote: The Hon'ble Ronald Reagan President of the United States of America Washington D.C.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: Soviet leader; signed INF agreement with Reagan

mentions.quote: your recent discussions with Mr. Gorbachev, particularly on the nuclear disarmament issue and the Afghanistan problem.

persons.name: Najibullah
persons.role: Afghan leader (PDPA), met Gandhi in Delhi during transit halt to Vietnam

mentions.quote: Mr. Najibullah and the PDPA are showing greater flexibility in approaching the political issues involved.

persons.name: Zahir Shah
persons.role: Former Afghan king in exile in Rome; India proposed continued discussions

mentions.quote: We have contacted King Zahir Shah in Rome and proposed continued discussions with him.

persons.name: Dean
persons.role: US Ambassador (to India) who delivered Reagan's letter

mentions.quote: Your letter was handed over to me by Ambassador Dean.

organizations.name: Soviet Union
organizations.notes: Committed to withdraw troops from Afghanistan.

organizations.name: Senate Appropriations Committee
organizations.notes: Proposed linking India and Pakistan nuclear programmes.

places.name: New Delhi
places.significance: Letter origin and site of Gandhi-Najibullah meeting.

places.name: Geneva
places.significance: Venue of forthcoming proximity talks on Afghanistan.

places.name: Stockholm
places.significance: Venue of summit of Six-Nation peace initiative.

places.name: Afghanistan
places.significance: Subject of Soviet withdrawal and settlement.

events.description: Rajiv Gandhi met Najibullah in Delhi during a transit halt on his way to Vietnam.
Gandhi's letter to Reagan on INF treaty, Afghanistan and the India-Pakistan nuclear issue.
Direction on Indo-US cooperation set in Washington DC.
Reagan and Gorbachev signed INF agreement at the Washington summit; Soviet commitment to withdraw from Afghanistan noted.
Gandhi writes to Reagan reporting on his meeting with Najibullah and Afghan policy.
Gandhi met Najibullah in Delhi during his transit halt en route to Vietnam.
Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF agreement eliminating short and medium-range nuclear weapons.
Planned Stockholm summit of the Six-Nation Five-Continent peace initiative.
Forthcoming proximity talks in Geneva on Afghanistan settlement.
Direction on Indo-US cooperation set in Washington DC on October 20.

relationships.quote: We look forward to continued close consultation and interaction with the United States in this process.

sources_cited: Reagan letter to Gandhi (referenced, delivered by Ambassador Dean)
key_claims: India urged a broad-based government in Afghanistan embracing all sections of opinion.
Najibullah told Gandhi that the Soviet withdrawal commitment created conditions for a peaceful settlement.
India sought contact with King Zahir Shah and other groups inside and outside Afghanistan.
Gandhi hoped Pakistan and Iran would adopt a constructive approach to the Afghanistan settlement.
Gandhi thanked Reagan for correcting the Senate Appropriations Committee's linking of Indian and Pakistani nuclear programmes.
